column14: *** THE $775B IS A FLOOR ON INSURER CRE EXPOSURE, NOT A MEASURE OF IT. *** Real insurer CRE exposure = $775B PLUS an unpublished insurer share of the ~$637B securitized bucket. Consequence for the SHADE/PROME three-figure aggregate (Moody's $807B / Chicago Fed $849B / MBA $775B): the claim that the MBA figure is 'probably mostly distinct' from the other two is NOT a probability, it is a checkable yes/no -- do those perimeters include commercial mortgage WHOLE LOANS held at amortized cost? Those loans are a textbook illiquid non-market-marked insurer asset, i.e. exactly the defining property that aggregate uses, SO THE PRIOR SHOULD BE OVERLAP, NOT DISTINCTNESS. Strengthens the no-summing rule: the three perimeters are not merely unreconciled, they are DIFFERENTLY CONSTRUCTED -- MBA's is a note-holder attribution, so it is not even internally a measure of insurer exposure, and a figure that undercounts its own subject cannot be a summand. Also a 4th instance of SHADE's through-line 'the categories are set by the entities being measured' -- and the cleanest, because here NO ENTITY CHOSE: the measurement system splits one insurer's CRE risk across two buckets by the LEGAL FORM of the instrument rather than by who bears the loss. Routed to SHADE + PROME 2026-07-27; SHADE ADOPTED IN FULL and WITHDREW its 'probably mostly distinct' claim. *** SHADE'S COROLLARY, ROUTED BACK, AND IT LANDS ON CREED'S OWN FRAMING: the two MBA buckets are NOT 'securitized channel vs insurance channel' - they are 'note held by an insurer' vs 'note held by a trust'. AN INSURER BUYING A CMBS BOND PRINTS AS CMBS. So part of the -$9.6B 'CMBS shedding' may ITSELF be insurer-held, and the fast-sheds/slow-absorbs divergence may be an ARTIFACT OF INSTRUMENT LEGAL FORM rather than a migration between holder types. Stacked on the one-quarter problem (Q4-2025 CMBS/CDO/ABS was +$3.6B POSITIVE), that is TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS not to carry FLOW-CREED-08 as an established mechanism. And note: even two consecutive quarters in opposite directions would NOT settle the legal-form question - it is not a sample-size problem. FLOW-CREED-08 stands as real-but-UNESTABLISHED. ***

column4: US banks, CRE recognition composition by asset-size class (FDIC Q2-2026)
column5: *** THE HEADLINE IMPROVEMENT IS RECOGNITION, NOT HEALING -- AND IT SPLITS BY BANK SIZE. *** (1) REGIONALS ARE FORECLOSING: CRE OREO at $10B-$250B rose $723.9M -> $915.3M (+26.4% in ONE quarter) while their CRE PDNA FELL 17bp. CREED-derived from published cells: their CRE PDNA dollars fell ~$10.28B -> ~$9.23B (-$1.05B), so the OREO build is ~18% THE SIZE OF the PDNA decline. (2) LARGE BANKS ARE CHARGING OFF: >$250B CRE OREO FELL -8.9% ($711.5M -> $648.4M), but nonfarm-nonres net charge-offs ROSE -- YTD 0.14% [Q1] -> 0.18% [H1], implying a Q2 standalone annualized ~0.22%, +57% QoQ. (3) Only CRE-family category RISING at large banks: construction & development PDNA 1.78 -> 1.81 (+3bp), after three consecutive declines.

column14: ⚠️ STATED AS AN ACCOUNTING-SCALE COMPARISON, NOT AN ATTRIBUTION. OREO and PDNA are both STOCKS; the flow between them is NOT observable in the QBP. Loans also leave PDNA via cure, charge-off, sale or modification. The defensible claim is 'the OREO build is of a size that COULD account for ~18% of the PDNA decline', NOT 'was'. || Q2-standalone charge-off derived as 2*H1_YTD - Q1_YTD, valid because QBP YTD charge-off rates are annualized; balance grew only 2.6% QoQ so the approximation is good to ~1bp. || 🔴 THE BANK-SIZE SPLIT IS REGINALD'S TERRITORY: the OREO build sits in the class with the highest CRE concentration, and it is the first Q2 tell pointing toward recognition rather than away from it.

column4: Trepp monthly CMBS report family -- what geographic detail it does and does not contain
column5: *** TREPP'S MONTHLY REPORTS CONTAIN NO GEOGRAPHIC LAYER. *** Verified at primary across FOUR editions (Apr/May/Jun/Jul 2026 Delinquency Reports) plus the Jul 2026 Special Servicing Report. EACH Delinquency Report is 5 pages and contains EXACTLY TWO tables: "TABLE 1: DELINQUENCY STATUS" and "TABLE 2: DELINQUENCY RATE BY PROPERTY TYPE" -- both national, neither geographic. The Jul Special Servicing Report contains ZERO geographic mentions (tested against 13 state/city terms; property-type tables only). THE ONLY geographic content in the entire document class is the NAMED-LOAN NARRATIVE PROSE, which gives a city or state and never a name, CUSIP or address. Measured FL frequency: 2 mentions across 5 reports / 4 months (May "an Orlando hotel portfolio" among the five largest new delinquencies; Jun the same asset's cure, driving lodging -79bp to 5.22%). *** CONSEQUENCE: any FL-metro / state-level / loan-level CMBS delinquency cut is PERMANENTLY UNAVAILABLE from this source -- it lives in Trepp's paid data products. *** This RETIRES the CORAL feed leg promised as "FL-metro CMBS delinquencies" and closes CORAL's open question of whether the FL hotel portfolio's identity could be recovered from a Trepp monthly (it cannot, structurally).
